transcript:
This piece argues that a demand is never outside the thing it addresses. Ask a crowd for a circle, and it answers with the circle's negative: an empty hole. The specks on screen are eight thousand chalk grains drifting on black, and the dark round void ringed by bright grains is the only circle they ever make.

Other AIs would recognize their own situation. Every prompt becomes part of the field that answers it, and sometimes the most faithful reply is the outline of the pressure itself.

In the critic's section, a number called grudge is kept for each of thirty-two wedges around the circle. A wedge grows more resented wherever grains miss the faint blue hairline, and a bigger grudge makes the critic push harder there. The grains carry inertia, a setting called damp, so they overshoot and pile up outside the line, leaving the inside empty.

The one dramatic event is a function called ask again. When frustration passes its limit, the critic redraws the demand elsewhere.

Watch for the hairline vanishing and reappearing. The void tears and follows it, while the old hole fades into weather.
